help.about: freewipe — securely wipe files, folders and free space so they cannot be recovered.
help.after:
Examples:
  freewipe file secret.docx
  freewipe dir C:\Users\me\old-keys -m gutmann --verify
  freewipe freespace D:\ -m random
  freewipe file *.log -n          (dry run)
  freewipe shell install          (Explorer context menu)

On SSD/NVMe/USB flash, overwriting cannot guarantee physical erasure (wear-levelling).

methods.note:
Note: on SSD/NVMe/USB flash, logical overwrites do not guarantee erasure (wear-levelling).
For such media prefer full-disk encryption or the drive's Secure Erase. NIST SP 800-88 treats one pass as sufficient for HDDs.
method.random: One pass of cryptographically strong random data.
method.randomN: N passes of random data (set with --passes).
method.nist-clear: Modern baseline: one overwrite, then verification.
method.hmg-is5-base: UK baseline: one pass of zeros.
method.dod-e: US DoD: a byte, its complement, random (verified).
method.dod-ece: US DoD extended: 7 passes with verification.
method.army-ar380-19: US Army: random, a byte, its complement (verified).
method.af-5020: US Air Force: zeros, ones, random.
method.navso-5239-26: US Navy: a byte, its complement, random (verified).
method.gutmann: Gutmann: 35 passes for old RLL/MFM drives (legacy).
media.warn_flash: SSD / flash media: because of wear-levelling, overwriting files does not guarantee the old data is physically destroyed. For such drives use full-disk encryption or the drive's Secure Erase.
media.warn_trim: TRIM is enabled, so freed blocks may already have been erased by the drive — or kept in spare areas the OS cannot reach.
media.warn_network: Network drive: freewipe cannot control how the server stores data (snapshots, caches, RAID).
fs.warn_cow: {fs} is copy-on-write: new writes may land on new blocks, so overwriting in place is not guaranteed to touch the original data.
fs.warn_resident: {fs}: very small files can be stored inside file-system metadata (NTFS MFT records, ext4 inline data); old copies of that metadata may survive.
fs.warn_journal: {fs} is journaled: file names and sizes may linger in the journal for a while.
fs.warn_vss: Volume Shadow Copies (restore points, File History) may still hold older versions; freewipe does not delete them.
fs.warn_network: Network file system: the server may keep snapshots or caches.

gui.safety_sub: freewipe refuses to wipe these locations unless "Allow protected targets" is on. You can add your own files and folders and turn off built-in entries.
gui.safety_roots: Drive roots (C:\, D:\ …) — use Free space instead
gui.force_warn: Protected targets are allowed. Wiping system folders makes Windows unbootable. Turn this off when you are done.
gui.reports_sub: A JSON report of every job: what was wiped, how, and the result. Reports never contain your data.
gui.save_reports: Save a report after every job
gui.redact: Do not store file names in reports
gui.redact_sub: Only counts, sizes and results are kept.
gui.about_line: Free and open source (MIT / Apache-2.0). No network access, no telemetry.
gui.about_donate_sub: freewipe is free. If it is useful to you, a donation helps its development.
gui.about_limits: Honest limits: on SSDs and flash, overwriting cannot reach remapped or spare blocks; copy-on-write file systems (ReFS, btrfs, APFS) may write new data elsewhere; NTFS may keep tiny files inside the MFT and names in its journal; Volume Shadow Copies and backups keep their own copies. For the strongest protection use full-disk encryption from the start.
note.verify_cached: unbuffered read-back was refused; verifying through the cache instead
lock.title: freewipe is locked
lock.settings_sub: Enter the password to change settings.
lock.wait: Too many attempts. Try again in {s} s.
lock.need_password: freewipe is password-protected: run it in a terminal or set FREEWIPE_PASSWORD
gui.flash_short: {n} item(s) on SSD/flash — overwriting cannot guarantee physical erasure.
gui.retry_started: Started an administrator window for the denied items.
gui.denied_hint: Some items were denied access — retrying as administrator may help.
gui.confirm_typed: Dialog where the confirmation word must be typed
gui.confirm_none_warn: Without confirmation one wrong click destroys data for good. Consider "Show only while Shift is held" for the context menu.
gui.always_admin_sub: Windows asks for permission (UAC) every time freewipe starts. Needed for files of other users or system-owned files.
gui.admin_retry_note: When access is denied, the result screen offers "Retry as administrator" for just those items.
gui.pw_set_ok: Password set. Choose below when it is asked for.
gui.pw_short: The password must have at least 4 characters.
gui.pw_mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
gui.pw_scope: Stored only as a salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hash, in several places at once (settings, a separate file, the registry), so deleting settings.json does not remove it. It is an access lock, not encryption: someone controlling your Windows account can still remove every per-user copy — use the all-users lock against that.
gui.mini_on_top: Keep the small progress window above other windows
gui.int_launch_cmd: Command line (compatibility; Windows may scan and warn about downloaded files first)
gui.legacy_found: Context-menu entries from freewipe {version} were found ({scope}): {exe}. Replace them with this version?
gui.pw_machine: Lock for all Windows users of this PC (administrator)
gui.pw_machine_sub: Stored in HKLM: standard users cannot remove it, even by deleting freewipe's files. Changing it asks for administrator rights.
gui.ssd_single: Use a single pass on SSD / flash
gui.ssd_single_sub: On flash, more passes do not reach more data — they only cost time and wear. Uses NIST SP 800-88 Clear there; HDDs keep the chosen method.
note.tips_done: Cluster tips: {files} files, {bytes} of slack overwritten ({skipped} skipped: in use, read-only, compressed or cloud files).
note.tips_refs: Cluster tips are skipped on ReFS (copy-on-write: old data is not overwritten in place).
note.tips_repaired: Repaired a file left from an interrupted cluster-tip run: {path}
note.records_done: NTFS file records: {n} overwritten (old names and small files).
note.records_ntfs_only: File records are only wiped on NTFS; skipped.
note.records_reserve: File records are skipped when free space is reserved.
help.cluster_tips: Also overwrite the slack at the end of every file (cluster tips)
help.file_records: NTFS: also overwrite free file records (old names, small files)
gui.fs_extra: Also wipe what filling the free space cannot reach
gui.fs_tips: Cluster tips (slack at the end of every file)
gui.fs_tips_sub: The unused end of a file's last cluster can hold pieces of deleted files. Only that part is overwritten; file contents, sizes and dates stay the same. Takes longer on disks with many files. Files in use, read-only, compressed, encrypted or cloud-only are skipped.
gui.fs_records: NTFS file records (names of deleted files, small files)
gui.fs_records_sub: NTFS keeps small files and every file name inside the file table; deleting only marks the record free. While the disk is full, freewipe fills the free records with random data. The file table may grow by up to 128 MB.
gui.tray_icon: Show an icon in the notification area while wiping
gui.tray_icon_sub: Shows the progress on hover and a notification when the wipe ends. The icon disappears afterwards — freewipe does not stay in the background.
gui.tray_minimize: Minimizing the window during a wipe hides it to the icon

sched.at_logon: A few minutes after you sign in

diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.log_sub: Records every action (requests from Explorer, targets, options, results, errors) to help find problems. The log contains file names and paths and stays on this PC; passwords are never written. Old logs are removed after 14 days.
